articleTitle: Research on the Optimization Control Strategy of the Four-Quadrant Rectifiers for High-Speed EMUs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The four-quadrant rectifier is an important component of electric multiple units (EMUs), and the optimization of its control strategy is a hot spot. First, this paper introduces the traditional control strategy and explores the influence of the presence or absence of the secondary filter circuit and dualization on the working performance of the rectifier. Second, for the issues of grid-side harmonics and DC-side voltage overshoot in the rectifier, an improved the voltage outer loop of the transient direct current control strategy is proposed. A low-pass is introduced filter to suppress the secondary ripple on the DC side and reduce the grid-side harmonics. The traditional PI control is improved as a single-neuron PID to reduce the DC-side voltage overshoot. Finally, Simulation analysis was carried out to verify that the optimized control strategy in this paper can achieve the control goals of DC-side voltage, small grid-side current harmonics, and high-power factors of grid-side voltage and current.

articleTitle: Ring Topology Drive for Seven-Phase Switched Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Traditional multiphase switched reluctance motor (SRM) power converters have issues such as a large number of power devices and motor terminals, as well as large size and high cost of the converter. To address these problems, this paper investigates a novel seven-phase interphase series excitation switched reluctance motor system drive topology. The working principle of the switched reluctance motor is introduced. Focusing on two operational modes: two-phase overlapping conduction and four-phase overlapping conduction, two ring drive topologies are proposed. A comparative analysis is conducted on the impact of two-phase overlapping conduction and four-phase overlapping conduction on the motor output torque when applying ring drive topologies. A 14/8 structured seven-phase prototype is used as the control object, and simulations are carried out on the proposed power converter under the current chopping control strategy. The simulation results are comparatively studied.

articleTitle: Black Start Scheme for Grid-Forming Doubly Fed Wind Turbines with Improved Virtual Synchronous Control Based on Virtual Stator Electromotive Force
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: After a power outage in the grid with a high proportion of new energy access, the black start is required to restore the power supply quickly. However, in the early stage of black start, the strength of the power system is weak, and only using grid following vector control methods cannot support doubly fed induction generators (DFIGs) to achieve black start. Therefore, a grid-forming control strategy with current dual loop control based on virtual synchronous generator (VSG) to construct virtual stator electromotive force (EMF) is proposed, and a corresponding wind turbine (WT) black start process is formulated. Moreover, the WT reduced the impact of wind speed fluctuations on system stability by limiting output power. The simulation results using MATLAB/Simulink demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed black start strategy and process. Meanwhile, under the dual influence of load disturbances and wind speed fluctuations, the wind turbine stabilizes the system frequency and voltage within the allowable range for the black start.

articleTitle: Robustness Sensorless Control Strategy for PMSM Based on MPC with Multi-parameter Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: This paper presents a robust sensorless control based on model predictive control (MPC) with multi-parameter estimation. To obtain the precision rotor position against the variation of parameters, the inductance and permanent-magnet flux parameters have been estimated by the model reference adaptive system, and the adaptive super twisting observer is adopted to identify the resistance parameter. Meanwhile, the identified parameters are participated in magnetic flux observer to obtain the rotor position. Moreover, the multi-parameter estimation results updated in MPC can reject all parameter mismatches; thereby, the robustness of the control system can be enhanced. Finally, the simulation result validates the proposed technology.

articleTitle: A Natural Fault-Tolerant Control for a Dual Three-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor with Single-Phase Open Fault
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The Dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor (DT-PMSM) has gained widespread application in high-reliability scenarios owing to its high power density and exceptional fault-tolerant capabilities. Single-phase failures are a common occurrence in electric drives. In addressing the open-phase fault-tolerant control of multi-phase motors, a reduced-order decoupled model is frequently formulated; nevertheless, the associated decoupled matrices are susceptible to variations based on the opened-phase, rendering them unsuitable for industrial applications. To address these challenges, this research introduces a natural fault tolerant control approach that utilizes the decoupling transformation matrices of the healthy mode consistently, regardless of the opened-phase. Furthermore, a comprehensive fault tolerant current re-configuration and regulation methodology is presented, incorporating controllability re-matching and constraints for equal amplitude and minimal copper losses. Experimental outcomes validate the efficacy and practicality of the proposed natural fault tolerant control strategy.

Author Keywords: dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Flux Controllable Reactor Access System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: In order to overcome the limitation that the inductance value of the conventional reactor changes in the power system, a new type of flux controllable reactor access system stability analysis is studied in this paper. Firstly, the topology and working principle of the flux controllable reactor are introduced, and the change of the equivalent impedance of the controllable reactor under the condition of actual injection signal delay is analyzed. The research shows that the delay has great influence on the equivalent impedance of the controllable reactor, and the equivalent impedance of the reactor may show negative resistance characteristics according to the difference of the delay time. Especially when there is a resistive load, the system may have resonance phenomenon, resulting in abnormal increase of the power grid current, and then cause the wrong operation of the relay protection device, which needs to take corresponding suppression measures. Secondly, the influence of delay on the stability of flux-controlled reactor access system is discussed. The correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified by theoretical analysis and simulation model. The research results provide an important reference for the stable application of flux controllable reactor in power system, and help to improve the stability and reliability of power system.

articleTitle: Circulating Current Suppression in Parallel Inverter System with Small Shared Inductance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: To accommodate low-voltage and high-power application scenarios, the parallel connection of multiple inverters has received widespread attention due to its ability to effectively increase the system capacity without enhancing the power level of the power electronics. Nevertheless, the application of multiple parallel structures can cause the circulating current problem, which affects the power quality and even endangers the stable operation of the system in serious cases. Therefore, the circulating current suppression becomes an urgent problem to be tackled. According to the characteristics of circulating current, this paper distinguishes it into the zero-sequence circulating current and the cross-circulating current, combs out the flow paths of both of them and establishes mathematical models respectively. Following that, a circulating current suppression strategy based on proportional-integral-resonant controller is proposed to effectively reduce the adverse effects of circulating current on the system operation. At last, a simulation is built in MATLAB/Simulink platform to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: A Novel DC Transformer Based 3RSC for DC Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: DC transmission technology and DC grid technology is one of the effective technical ways to solve the offshore wind power delivery system, high-voltage and large-capacity DC transformer is the key equipment to connect different voltage levels of DC grid. Firstly, this paper presents a novel DC transformer based on 3RSC (Triple Voltage Resonant Switched Capacitor Converter) module for interconnecting turbine output with medium voltage collection network. Secondly, an analysis of the working principle of the 3RSC module and the energy transfer principle of the transformer is presented, and a control strategy is also given. Finally, the feasibility was verified by a simulation through MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Coordinated Operation Methods of MGP for Stability Ability Improvement of Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: To address the issue of reduced stability in high-proportion renewable energy grids caused by the weak support of grid-connected new energy power electronics, some scholars have proposed the Motor-Generator Pair (MGP) grid-connection technology. This technology enables renewable energy units to connect to the grid through a real synchronous machine interface, actively providing frequency and voltage support to the grid. Although some theoretical and experimental research on MGP has been conducted, there is still a lack of field operation experience and complete systems. Focusing on the operational issues of integrating MGP systems into actual microgrids, this paper, based on an application case, studies the coordinated operation methods and devices for integrating MGP into specific microgrid. A coordinated control method for MGP systems in microgrids is proposed in this paper, achieving control over MGP transmission power and stable grid-connection. Additionally, a 10kW MGP grid-connection device has been developed, and its feasibility has been verified through experiments.

articleTitle: Investigation of Losses in the Integrated Charger by Using Variable Flux Reluctance Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: In order to reduce the cost and size of the on-board charger, it is proposed by using the integrated charger, which uses the multi-functional motor driver system for the battery charging. In this paper, an isolated integrated charger based on variable flux reluctance machine (VFRM) is investigated in terms of losses, since high efficiency is required for the integrated battery charger. Thus, in the paper the loss of the multi-functional VFRM at different frequencies with/without load will be investigated. Moreover, the losses in the converter are analyzed so as to explore the overall efficiency of the charging system, which can help to maximize the overall efficiency. For verification, a 12/10 VFRM was built and tested. It shows that at switch frequency of 20kHz, the overall loss of the integrated charging system is lowest.

articleTitle: Improved MFAC-based Re-flight Control Method for Power Inspection Flying Wall-climbing Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: In recent years, ground robots designed for power emergency inspections have faced challenges in terms of maneuverability and visibility, often being outperformed by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). However, UAVs themselves are limited by short duration capabilities, preventing prolonged monitoring of issues. Existing claw-spiked flying wall-climbing robots, while capable of landing, struggle with re-flying due to their reliance on open-loop control systems. This paper introduces a Modified Fractional-order Adaptive Control-Proportional Integral Derivative (MFAC-PID) control algorithm. A dynamic model for the re-flying process was analyzed and established, optimizing the re-flying control algorithm accordingly. Simulation and experimental results confirm the effectiveness of this approach in controlling re-flying, thereby addressing the aforementioned issues.

articleTitle: DC Arc Fault Detection Method Based on Lightweight Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: As the global demand for low-carbon energy continues to grow, photo voltaic (PV) power generation is gradually becoming a dominant form of renewable energy. Due to the frequent occurrence of electrical fires caused by PV systems, most of which are related to DC arc faults, the safety of PV systems, particularly the prevention and detection of DC arc faults, has become an urgent issue that needs to be addressed. Achieving efficient and accurate detection of DC arc faults is a key focus of current PV system safety research. This paper proposes a DC arc fault detection system based on a lightweight neural network. The system only extracts the amplitude of the frequency band with the most obvious arc features from the FFT decomposition results of the signal as input and utilizes a depthwise separable convolutional neural network to reduce computational complexity while maintaining strong feature extraction capabilities, thereby meeting the real-time detection requirements of embedded systems. We conducted experimental validation using the STM32H745 development board, and the results showed that the system performed excellently in detecting arc faults, achieving a detection accuracy of 99.39%. It also maintained an extremely low false alarm rate while almost never missing any faults. Additionally, the system demonstrated good robustness when dealing with complex environments and current fluctuations.

Author Keywords: DC arc fault;lightweight neural network;real-time detection;FFT decomposition; embedded system

articleTitle: Research on Control Strategy of PMSM Based on Duty Cycle Tracking SHEPWM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: For high-speed or high-power drive systems, limited by the switching frequency allowed by the inverter, asynchronous space vector pulse-width modulation (ASVPWM) results in higher low-order harmonics. These harmonics can be reduced by selective harmonic elimination pulse-width modulation (SHEPWM). This paper adopts SHEPWM closed-loop implementation method based on field-oriented control (FOC). However, the switching angle of SHEPWM is obtained based on the fundamental current, resulting in an imbalance in volt-second product between the current regulator and inverter output employing SHEPWM during the sampling period, which seriously affects the control response of the system. To overcome this problem, this paper adjusts SHEPWM switching time based on the duty cycle of current controller, and eliminates the duty cycle deviation between them. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Speed Ripple Minimization of Open-Winding Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine Under Demagnetization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The open-winding permanent magnet synchronous machines have been widely used in many industrial applications due to their high torque density, high efficiency, wide constant power speed ratio (CPSR), and enhanced fault-tolerant capability. The permanent magnet (PM) materials used in these machines may suffer from irreversible demagnetization due to high operating temperature, short circuit faults, and vibration. This creates asymmetry in the air gap flux density, which induces additional harmonics in the back-EMF. These additional harmonics increase the torque ripple, which is reflected in the speed of the machine, especially at low operating speeds. The speed ripple increases the vibration, resulting in poor performance. This paper aims to minimize these speed ripples under partial demagnetization. A resonant controller is added in parallel with the conventional proportion-integral (PI) speed controller to suppress the speed ripples. The proposed algorithm is verified both in simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Synchronization Stability Analysis of Fractional-Order Virtual Synchronous Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The traditional virtual synchronous generator(VSG)control strategy provides virtual damping and inertia for the inverter in grid-connected operation, thereby enhancing the frequency and voltage support capability of the system. Nevertheless, the incorporation of virtual inertia will elevate the order of the system, engendering an oscillation in the output active power during the grid-connected operation of the inverter. Furthermore, the virtual inertia and damping will impede the responsiveness of the system. In light of the aforementioned analysis of the frequency domain characteristics of the fractional-order virtual inertia link, this paper puts forth a fractional-order virtual inertia virtual synchronous generator control strategy. Furthermore, the control strategy is employed to examine the equal area rule with fractional order, utilising the fault limit clearing time angle as a metric to assess the system's margin for large disturbance (transient) synchronisation. Additionally, the influencing factors of VSG transient synchronisation stability are investigated. The transient synchronisation stability of a fractional-order VSG system is investigated through the implementation of the proposed control strategy, with the simulation results corroborating the enhanced transient synchronous stability afforded by the strategy.

articleTitle: A Low-carbon Microgrid Evaluation Index System Adapted to the New Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Microgrids are key to the new power system, requiring effective low-carbon assessment across the “generation-grid-load-storage” spectrum. This paper proposes a carbon accounting method tailored to microgrid components and develops an evaluation index system to meet power system needs. Simulations demonstrate the system's effectiveness by comparing results before and after optimization.

articleTitle: Study on the Weakening of Cogging Torque by Stator Structure Optimization of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Since there is a large cogging torque in built-in permanent magnet synchronous motors, this paper analyzes the reasons for its generation. Simulations are carried out using finite element software to investigate the feasibility of reducing the cogging torque by combining auxiliary slots in the stator teeth and embedding magnetic slot wedges in the stator slots. The number, orientation and radius of the auxiliary slots in the stator teeth and the embedding of the magnetic slot wedges in the stator slots are determined through variable parameterization. Finally, the comparison of the values of the motor before and after optimization shows that reasonable opening of auxiliary slots and embedding of magnetic slot wedges can reduce the cogging torque of the motor.

articleTitle: Design of Variable Speed Three-Phase PMSM Series IE6 Efficiency Class
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The maximum efficiency class of variable speed AC motor stipulated by IEC is IE5, but at present, design and manufacture of a series of products (frame number 80~355, IP55, IC416) of IE6(above IE5) efficiency classified variable speed three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor or permanent magnet-assisted synchronous reluctance motor can be realized. This paper introduces the suggestions of IE6 efficiency classification, design method and design principles of three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor series products, and finally verifies the feasibility of serial design through prototype trial production and test, which provides a reference for the determination and design of IE6 variable-speed motor efficiency classification.

articleTitle: A DC Fault Clearance Device for Long-distance Offshore Wind Power DC Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: This paper proposes a DC fault clearance device for long-distance offshore wind power DC transmission system under DC short-circuit faults. With the proposed DC clearance device, the DCCB (DC circuit breaker) can be replaced by HSS (high-speed switch). Thus, the construction cost of the DC transmission grid can be saved. The topology and the working principle of the proposed device are analyzed in this paper. The equivalent fault circuits are constructed and the equation of fault current is deduced. This paper also proposes the protect scheme of the offshore wind power DC transmission system with fault clearance device. The effectiveness of the DC fault clearance device and the control strategy are validated by simulations on MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Indirect Carbon Emission Decomposition Technology of Industrial Load Electricity Based on Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Accurate and comprehensive measurement and analysis of carbon emissions in power systems are crucial for quantifying carbon footprints associated with electricity use, identifying the potential for carbon reduction across the entire system, and guiding industrial consumers in achieving interactive carbon reduction strategies. Currently, there are challenges such as the lack of fairness in calculating the indirect carbon emissions (IDCE) from power systems, ambiguity in the IDCE from internal electricity consumption by industrial users, and the high costs associated with production, operation, and maintenance. To address these issues, this paper introduces an energy meter-based method for measuring IDCE of industrial users, grounded in carbon flow theory. Direct carbon emissions from the power generation sector are allocated to industrial users based on the metered values of actual electricity meters, while the IDCE from the internal equipment of industrial users are determined using non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) technology. Furthermore, the feasibility and practicality of this method have been validated through numerical simulations during the initial planning phase of a pilot project in a city within Jiangsu Province. This has provided valuable insights and experience for future large-scale experiments and applications.

articleTitle: Effect of Stator Auxiliary Groove on the Vibration and Noise of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: In order to reduce the vibration and noise of the motor, this paper takes a to-slot 8-pole surface-mount permanent magnet synchronous motor as an example, uses Ansys Maxwell simulation software to analyze the electromagnetic field finite element analysis, analyzes the influence on the cogging torque, torque ripple and spatial harmonics from the geometer auxiliary groove shape, number of grooves, groove width and groove depth, determines the structural parameters of the auxiliary groove, conducts modal simulation analysis, and compares the vibration displacement and noise before and after optimization.

articleTitle: Enhancing Bus Stability Through LADRC Strategies for Energy Storage in Wave Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: In wave energy generation technology, a hybrid energy storage system is utilized to smooth DC bus voltage fluctuations. However, under the traditional PI control strategy, the stability of the DC bus voltage is vulnerable to disturbances, sudden load changes, and fluctuations. This paper proposes a self-resistant control method designed to effectively suppress bus voltage fluctuations while ensuring stable operation of the bidirectional DC/DC converter within the energy storage system. To deeply analyze the influencing factors in wave power generation energy storage systems, we establish a small signal model for the bidirectional DC/DC converter. PI control is applied to the current loop, and linear self-immunity control is employed for the voltage loop. System control equations are derived, and a control block diagram and transfer function are established. System parameter tuning and stability analysis are guided by Bode's plot and zero-pole plot methodologies. Simulation and experimental results verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the bidirectional DC/DC converter's self-immunity control strategy when applied to hybrid energy storage systems in wave energy generation technology.

articleTitle: PMSM Inter-Turn Short Circuit Fault Diagnosis Based on WOA-VMD
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The safety and reliability of the motor is the basis and guarantee of the stable operation of the motor, so it is of great significance to be able to quickly and accurately diagnose the early motor faults to avoid unnecessary downtime or even more serious consequences due to motor faults. In this paper, we diagnose the early inter-turn short-circuit fault of the motor from the two aspects of motor fault modeling and early fault signal processing. As the early fault signal of the motor is not obvious, we use the Variable Modal Decomposition (VMD) algorithm to process the fault signal, and use the whale optimization algorithm (WOA) to optimize the parameters of the VMD algorithm. After simulation verification results show that the best combination of parameters obtained after the whale optimization algorithm is applied to the VMD algorithm to decompose the fault signal, which can effectively eliminate the noise interference to extract the fault characteristics.

Author Keywords: Permanent magnet synchronous motor fault diagnosis

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Model of Position Servo PMSM Based on Finite Element and Loss Mapping Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Energy consumption model is an important basis for energy optimization of trajectory planning and energy efficiency evaluation of design scheme of position servo permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM), and its accuracy directly affects the actual optimization effect. This paper proposes a position servo PMSM energy consumption model based on finite element and loss mapping functions. Firstly, the deficiencies in the accuracy of loss calculation of existing typical energy consumption models are analyzed, and the simplified mapping relationship of losses is established based on the working curve of PMSM under traj ectory planning. Then, the loss data of PMSM is calculated through electromagnetic finite element, the trust-region algorithm is used to solve the optimal loss mapping function, and the energy consumption model is established. Finally, the energy consumption of position servo PMSM under trajectory planning is simulated and verified by experiment. The results show that compared with the traditional models, the proposed method simplifies the energy consumption model while reducing the error by 3.3% to 14.1 %. The method can be widely applied to position servo PMSM.

articleTitle: Analysis of Energy Efficiency Characteristics of Gravity Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Gravity energy storage (GES) has the advantages of high environmental adaptability, long life, high environmental protection, which have attracted the attention of more and more scholars in recent years. Efficiency is one of the key technical indicators for the large-scale promotion of energy storage. Since GES is in its infancy and the system structure is complex, the detailed and engineering practical analysis of the efficiency of GES is still in a blank stage. In response to the above problems, this paper proposes a method for establishing an efficiency simulation model. This model is based on the mechanical and electrical combination of the heavy block driving torque within the typical structure of GES. Through simulation analysis, the efficiency characteristics and the law of the loss ratio of the system are revealed: GES typical structure is rated at about 76%, of which the mechanical link loss accounts for the largest proportion of about 61 %, and the loss has a linear characteristic, while the single equipment motor loss is the largest, about 39%, and the loss of a single equipment is sorted from large to small as: motor, gearbox, chain, heavy block, drum and coupling.

articleTitle: User Identification in Low-Voltage Distribution Networks Using Support Vector Machine and Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Accurate identification of users within the low-voltage distribution area directly impacts grid loss calculations, fault detection, and electricity supply safety. With the rise of smart grid technology and the increasing complexity of power grids, this task has become more challenging. This study addresses these challenges by focusing on user identification based on simultaneous electricity consumption data, aiming to minimize the impact of time synchronization issues and data quality problems. The research employs Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest (RF) algorithms to classify users across multiple substations, enhancing generalization and adaptability to different user types. To tackle the issue of missing data, three interpolation methods-spline interpolation, piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation (PCHIP), and improved Makima interpolation-are tested. The study reveals that the Makima interpolation method consistently achieves the lowest average error across various missing data ratios. Validation examples demonstrate that using the Makima interpolation method results in high classification accuracy for both SVM and RF classifiers, with RF showing superior performance.

articleTitle: Study of Circuit Breaker Operational State Based on CNN and Kurtogram Parallel Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: In order to quickly and accurately assess the operating state of power circuit breakers, this paper proposes a method for assessing the operating state of power circuit breakers based on parallel acceleration of CNN and Kurtogram (CK). Firstly, the method takes spectral kurtosis as the core idea and uses the spectral kurtogram as a single input to the algorithm. Then, Kurtogram is used as a signal preprocessing technique to assist the model to better understand the characteristics of the signal by extracting the nonlinear components in the signal. Using the results of the Kurtogram calculation as a single feature of the CNN model helps to enhance the feature learning ability of the neural network model on the signal. Finally, to improve the model training speed and efficiency, this paper uses parallel acceleration to further accelerate the convergence speed of the algorithm and improve the overall training efficiency. In the validation phase, this paper uses vibration features for validation, and the results show that the method exhibits good characteristics and the accuracy of the CK method reaches 98.8%.

articleTitle: Stability Research on Back-to-Back Electric Spring Based on Impedance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: As a fast and automatic demand-side response technology, the topology of the electric spring has been continuously improved, among which the back-to-back electric spring omits the energy storage element on the DC side and exhibits better voltage regulation capability. In this paper, the back-to-back electric spring is used as the research object to analyze the impedance characteristics and stability of the system in the face of bidirectional power flow. Firstly, small signal models and impedance models are established for each port converter in the system. Meanwhile, the difference in impedance characteristics of each port converter under forward and reverse power is analyzed comparatively. The stability of the system on the DC and AC sides is studied through the Nyquist criterion. The impact of output power changes on system impedance characteristics and stability is also analyzed. The research results indicate that when power is transmitted in the forward direction, the negative impedance characteristics of the DC and AC terminals of the series electric spring module in the low-frequency range may cause system instability. Additionally, there is a bidirectional power stability discrepancy between the DC and AC sides of the back-to-back electric spring system.

articleTitle: Multi-physics Field Coupling Simulation of Vibration and Noise in the Three-dimensional Wound Core Reactors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: High voltage shunt reactors are important equipment for compensating reactive power in substations. Due to the iron core structure, traditional laminated iron core reactors have serious vibration and noise problems, which even affect their service life. However, the three-dimensional wound core reactor has significant advantages in energy saving, environmental protection, vibration, and noise reduction. Therefore, it is urgent to research the vibration and noise characteristics of three-dimensional wound iron core reactors. This article constructs a three-dimensional core reactor model based on multi-physics fields finite element simulation. Under rated operating conditions, the reactor's magnetic field, vibration, and noise distribution are calculated. It is found that the main frequency of reactor vibration noise at rated voltage is 100Hz. Meanwhile, due to the nonlinearity of the iron core, vibration noise has high-frequency harmonic components with multiples of 100Hz. In addition, under rated power frequency, the noise of the three-dimensional wound core reactor is 57.06 dB(A), which is significantly lower than that of laminated core reactors. This simulation study provides a theoretical basis for the vibration and noise reduction of the reactors.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculation and Reduction of Circulating Current Losses in SPM Motors Based on Conductor Turn Division Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: In this paper, a method of dividing the number of turns of conductor is presented and the loss of circulating current in winding is analyzed. The proposed method emphasizes considering the magnetic flux density distribution within motor slots, allowing for rapid allocation conductors while reducing circulating current losses. First, the magnetic flux density within the slots is extracted using the finite element method. Next, the effect of conductor spacing is taken into account, and K-means clustering is applied for the initial distribution of the stranded coils. The Hungarian algorithm is then used to consider the impact of slot magnetic flux density on the winding process. Then, the magnetic flux density at the center of the conductors is extracted according to their arrangement. The magnetic flux density is utilized in the analytical calculation of circulating current losses. Finally, compared with the finite element method, this strategy can suppress the circulation current loss while maintaining the shape of the stranded coil.

articleTitle: Optimal Design and Analysis of Homopolar Doubly Salient Permanet Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: A novel homopolar doubly salient permanent magnet (HDSPM) motor is presented, which has the special structure with the inner and outer of stator and rotor and the inner and outer of air gap. In order to reduce the cogging torque of the motor, eliminate the axial pulsation of the permanent magnet to the rotor and increase the utilization ratio of the material, the structural parameters of the 12/8 pole HDSPM motor are optimized. Three dimensional field circuit coupling simulation model is constructed, and the no-load characteristics, external characteristics and power characteristics of the new generator are studied according to different power generation methods. Finally, two methods are used to compare and analyze the core loss of HDSPM motor. The finite element simulation results show that the homopolar axial flux doubly salient motor has the characteristics of small torque ripple, low core loss and high power density, which provides a theoretical basis for further research.

Author Keywords: Homopolar doubly salient permanent magnet (HDSPM) motor

articleTitle: Improve the MTPA Performance of a Sensorless IPMSM Drive Based on On-Line Inductance Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: During the operation of an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) using maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control, changes in parameters can cause the optimal torque-current characteristic curve to deviate. In this paper, based on a modified high frequency square wave injection scheme, simultaneous rotor position and on-line inductance estimation are achieved. The identified inductance values are then applied to the MTPA control to correct the current vector angle, and the optimization results are consistent with theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Grid-forming Control of VSC-HVDC System with Offshore Wind Farm Integration and Direct-mounted Battery Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: For remote offshore wind farms (OWFs), using voltage source converter-based high voltage direct current (VSC-HVDC) transmission to integrate into the grid is a promising solution. To enhance the fault ride-through and grid support capabilities of VSC-HVDC systems with OWFs integration, a direct-mounted battery energy storage system (BESS) is installed on the DC side of the receiving end converter (REC). The BESS is controlled to absorb the excessive wind power during grid faults instead of braking resistors. Moreover, a coordinated grid-forming strategy for the VSC-HVDC system with OWFs and the BESS is proposed in this paper. The DC-link voltage dynamics is utilized in the REC to synchronize with the grid without using the phase-locked-loop (PLL) and deliver the grid frequency to the BESS and the OWFs autonomously. On this basis, the BESS can provide frequency support to the grid and the offshore wind turbines without communication. Finally, a simulation model is built in PSCAD/EMTDC to verify the functions of the BESS, confirming its capability to enhance the frequency stability and help the grid fault ride-through of the VSC-HVDC system with OWFs integration.

articleTitle: Analysis on Harmonic Inductance in Modular Dual-Permanent Magnet-Excited Vernier Motor by Field Modulation Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: This article presents a method in analyzing the harmonic self-inductance in modular dual-permanent-magnet-excited vernier (DPMEV) motor based on the field modulation theory. The feature of single-phase magnetic field is first investigated to reveal the relationship between time harmonic and space harmonic. It is found that the dc component of self-inductance is mainly caused by dc component time harmonic. Then the harmonic self-inductance is separated in the modular motor. Lastly, the harmonic self-inductance in traditional DPMEV and modular are compared. It is found that the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> and 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order harmonic which produced the largest self-inductance in the traditional DPMEV motor reduced greatly in the modular motor.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis on Efficiency Influence Factors of Transmission Chain Slope Gravity Energy Storage System Based on Sobol Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Aiming at the coupling effect of various structural design parameters on the efficiency of the transmission chain slope gravity energy storage system (TCS-GESS), in order to clarify the influence degree of each parameter on the efficiency, an efficiency sensitivity analysis method of TCS-GESS based on Sobol method is proposed. Firstly, with the three parameters of slope angle, mass block running speed and mass as the basic variables, the loss of each link is analyzed according to the structure of the TCS-GESS, and the efficiency analytical expression containing only each system variable parameter is derived, and the simulation efficiency analysis of double parameter change is carried out. Secondly, the Sobol method is used to analyze the efficiency sensitivity, quantify the influence degree of each parameter, evaluate the quantitative index of the coupling relationship between each parameter, and sort them. The results show that the influence of each parameter is ranked as follows: mass block running speed > mass > slope angle. Therefore, in the scheme design, the system with slightly larger mass block running speed, medium mass and slightly smaller slope angle has better comprehensive benefits.

articleTitle: A Power Shock Mitigation Method of Gravity Energy Storage System Based on Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: To address the active power impact issue caused by the discrete characteristics of the energy storage medium in gravity energy storage systems, a power impact mitigation method based on sliding mode control is proposed. This method leverages the rapid power regulation capabilities of doubly-fed induction generators (DFIG) and the excellent dynamic performance of sliding mode control. A 2.0 MW DFIG gravity energy storage system simulation model was developed. Comparative simulations under two typical power variation scenarios demonstrate that the sliding mode control system significantly reduces adjustment time and eliminates overshoot in stator current and rotor speed, thereby substantially mitigating system impacts. These results validate the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Harmonic Analysis and Numerical Calculation of Stator Core Loss and Temperature Field for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: During the operation of the motor, losses will be generated, and these losses will escape through the form of heat, so that the internal temperature of the motor increases. Different loss calculation methods of the PMSM are studied in this paper. The results indicate that the calculation method with rotating magnetic field and harmonic influence is the most accurate method for the calculation of iron loss in the PMSM. In this paper, based on a 750W PMSM, temperature results and the experimental values were compared under the natural air-cooling condition. which verifies the reliability of the calculation method.

articleTitle: Power Smoothing Control Strategy of Gravity Energy Storage System Based on Mechanical Flywheel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: With the gradual popularization and application of gravity energy storage technology, how to smooth the power fluctuation caused by the frequent switching of mass blocks in gravity energy storage system is particularly important. The mechanical flywheel has simple structure and high energy conversion rate. It can respond to load demand in milliseconds and is suitable for frequent charge and discharge cycles. With the 37kW slope gravity energy storage system, this paper proposes a power smoothing control strategy for the gravity energy storage system, which determines the maximum speed and minimum speed of the mechanical flywheel by changing the ratio of the double reduction gear box, to match the inertia of the mechanical flywheel according to the mass of the mass block in the system. The results indicate that the use of mechanical flywheel can effectively smooth out the power fluctuation of the gravity energy storage system, which is a beneficial exploration for the technical application of the gravity energy storage system.

articleTitle: Economic and Reliability Optimization of Transformer Maintenance Strategies for Substation Asset Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Transformers are crucial components in modern power systems, enabling efficient long-distance power transmission and reliable power distribution. This paper proposes a novel approach to transformer maintenance by incorporating external degrees of freedom, aiming for overall optimization of substation assets. Methods for constructing transformer health indices and failure rate models are adopted in this study. An optimization problem for maintenance strategies based on economic reliability is formulated, and the proposed strategy is validated through a case study of a 500kV substation. The results demonstrate that by considering both transformer-specific conditions and interconnections between substation equipment, the proposed strategy could enhance the overall economic and reliability performance of power supply assets.

articleTitle: Parallel Fault Diagnosis Algorithm of Circuit Breaker Based on Arc Power Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The main function of the circuit breaker is to isolate the fault part of the power grid in time after the disconnection command is issued. A fault in the opening operation of the circuit breaker can result in a catastrophic event. Therefore, the fault detection of circuit breakers plays a vital role in the protection of power systems. This paper presents an algorithm for circuit breaker fault detection based on arc power loss. The power loss of the circuit breaker caused by the arc increases with the extension of the arc time, and the arc burning time increases with the failure caused by different reasons. There is a power loss between the input and output of the circuit breaker, and the power loss can be used to estimate the arc energy. Each time the estimated arc energy of the breaker opening operation reaches a predefined trip level, a trip signal is activated, and the absence of an interrupt current within the breaker's maximum allowable arc time indicates a fault in the breaker operation. Computer simulation studies to analyze the performance of the proposed technique show that the algorithm can distinguish between normal and abnormal arc energies and thus identify faults in circuit breakers.

articleTitle: High-precision Position Control of Ultrasonic Motor Based on Transient Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of the position control of the ultrasonic motor and give full play to its characteristics such as low speed, fast response and self-locking in case of power failure, this paper proposes a stepping control method of the ultrasonic motor based on the transient response. A digital ultrasonic motor controller based on DSP is designed. A high-precision angular displacement test-bed is built by combining the above controller, a high-precision absolute rotary encoder and the LabVIEW upper computer program. Taking traveling wave ultrasonic motor with 60mm in diameter as the control object, the influence of ultrasonic motor's driving parameters on the step angle under transient response is studied. The experimental results show that the minimum open-loop step angle of ultrasonic motor is less than 1” with good stability. In addition, in order to achieve fast and high-precision positioning control combined with the transient response characteristics of ultrasonic motor, a composite control algorithm of step control and traditional PID control is proposed. This control algorithm realizes the high-precision closed-loop position control of ultrasonic motor and the information exchange between the upper computer and the lower computer with fast response. The experimental results show that the maximum adj ustment time is 0.8s and the maximum positioning difference is less than or equal to 2.9” within 360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>.

articleTitle: Analysis of Loss of An Unevenly Distributed Rotor Induction Motor with Double-slot Sinusoidal Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: This paper proposes an unevenly distributed rotor induction motor with double-slot sinusoidal modulation to reduce the loss of induction motors due to the use of a skewed slot structure. The components of the loss of an induction motor are first analyzed and the formula for the calculation of each part of the loss is derived. The spatial position angle of the rotor, as well as the formula for calculating the width of the rotor slots, is determined for induction motors with double-slot sinusoidal modulation. This study employs two-dimensional finite element eddy current field simulation to comparatively analyze the losses in various parts of two different rotor configurations. The results demonstrate that the induction motor with a double-slot sinusoidally modulated unevenly distributed rotor and equal slot fits can effectively reduce losses and enhance the efficiency of the induction motor.

Author Keywords: unevenly distributed rotor induction motor with double slot sinusoidal modulation

articleTitle: Stability Analysis and Improvement of Symmetric PLL-Based VSC in Weak Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: For grid-connected voltage source converter (VSC) under weak grid conditions, frequency coupling caused by asymmetric system structure poses challenges for system modeling and controller design. Fortunately, frequency coupling can be eliminated by introducing a symmetrical Phase-locked loop (SPLL). Meanwhile, the employed SPLL can symmetrize the system model, transforming the complex multi-input multi-output (MIMO) system into a simpler single-input single-output (SISO) system. This paper derives an impedance model of grid-connected inverters with a symmetrical Phase-Locked Loop (SPLL). Analysis of the impedance characteristic using the impedance model established shows that the symmetrical PLL has a significant negative impact on system stability in weak grid. Moreover, a novel grid voltage feed-forward strategy is proposed to improve the stability of VSC under weak grid conditions. The effectiveness of the strategy has been validated through simulations.

articleTitle: Research on Smooth Switching Strategy of Two-Level SVPWM and SHEPWM Hybrid Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Multi-mode hybrid modulation is usually used in high-speed or high-power electric drives, and the smooth switching between different modulation strategies is very important for the safe and stable operation of the system. To solve this problem, the smooth switching strategy is studied in this paper, which takes into account the smooth switching of switching frequency of asynchronous modulation, the smooth switching between asynchronous modulation and synchronous modulation strategies, and the smooth switching between different synchronous modulation strategies with different pulse ratios. The above three kinds of switching cover almost all possible situations, so the presented strategy has strong universality. The effectiveness is verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Objective Optimization of Transformer Sequential Maintenance Strategy Considering Component Health Status
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: A multi-objective optimized sequential maintenance strategy that integrates the health status of key components of transformer is proposed in this paper to enhance the flexibility of maintenance strategies. The transformer body, bushings, cooling system, tap switch, and non-electric protection devices, which are five pivotal components, are individually assessed to analyze the overall condition of the transformer and are maintained in sequence according to their health status. Optimized maintenance sequences are searched to minimize the health index, risk value, and maintenance cost, which could effectively enhance the maintenance specificity and balance different metrics. The proposed method was validated through a practical case study.

articleTitle: Research on Loss Optimization of AC-Excitation Synchronous Condenser Under Multi-Condition Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: AC-Excitation Synchronous Condenser (AC SynCon), which has the ability to provide active and reactive power synchronously, shows great potential in the application of new energy power system. To minimize loss and meet the performance requirements of ACSynCon under multiple operating conditions, this paper proposes a multi-objective hierarchical optimization method. The loss under long-term no-load operation, long-term phase-lagging operation, and short-time tripled active overload operation are selected as the optimization objectives. Based on the proposed integrated sensitivity analysis of optimization parameters, parameter scanning method is adopted for the low integrated sensitivity parameters to obtain the optimal value. At the same time, finite element analysis is adopted to obtain the high integrated sensitivity parameters database for the Kriging surrogate model training. Finally, NSGA-II algorithm is used to optimize the Kriging surrogate model and finite element simulation is performed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Virtual Vector Modulation Strategy to Suppress the Third Harmonic of Common-Mode Voltage for Three-Level Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: For three-level inverters, there exists a control coupling between common-mode voltage (CMV) suppression and neutral point voltage (NPV) balancing. To address this issue, this paper proposes an Improved Varied Virtual Space Vector Modulation (I-VVSVM) strategy that effectively decouples CMV suppression from NPV balancing. By defining medium virtual vectors for NPV balancing and large virtual vectors for CMV suppression, the proposed I-VVSVM strategy can simultaneously reduce the amplitude of CMV and third harmonic content while maintaining balanced NPV. Finally, a simulation model for a Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) three-level inverter is developed using Matlab/Simulink to validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Based on Novel High-Order Logarithmic SMO and STPLL PMSM Position Sensorless Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Sliding mode observer (SMO) is widely used in sensorless control of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) due to its simple structure, strong robustness, and good control performance. However, SMO's inherent chattering can affect the system's control performance. A new high-order logarithmic sliding mode observer (NFHLSMO) is proposed for this purpose, which accurately estimates the back electromotive force and reduces system chattering. In addition, to improve the accuracy of speed estimation, a new method based on a novel Super-twisting control law was designed in the phase-locked loop to replace the PI loop, effectively optimizing the stator current, suppressing speed oscillations, and achieving accurate speed estimation. The results show that the position-free control strategy has good accuracy in speed estimation, dynamic performance, and robustness.

Author Keywords: New high-order logarithmic sliding mode observer
New type of super-twisting control law

articleTitle: Parameter Identified for Energy Storage Based on Terminal Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Recently, serious cyclical energy shortages have occurred in the global energy market, adjusting the existing energy structure has become the solution, and PV generation plays an important role in the renewable power system. But PV is a random system, it is necessary to add some battery energy storage system (BESS) to guarantee the system is safe and stable. The parameters in the BESS is the key part in the control. The paper adopts the sliding mode control (SMC) to design a terminal SMC observer to estimate the state of BESS, and can obtain the state of charging and recharging, to improve the safety of PV system. The simulation results verified the proposed method is effective.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method for Power Converter of SRG System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: An online diagnostic strategy for power converter fault of switched reluctance generator (SRG) system is proposed by detecting the integrated current information. The location of the employed current sensors for each phase winding is optimized. Preliminary fault confirmation is carried out by detecting the difference between the actual value and the estimated value of the current sensor. The failure type and failure device is located by detecting the deviation between the detection value and the estimated value of the installed current sensor. The effectiveness of the investigated method has been experimentally verified.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fuzzy Sliding Mode for Sensorless Control with Performance Enhancement in PMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The position sensors of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) will restrict the wide application of PMSMs in industry due to their own limitations. Thus, the promotion of sensorless control will greatly improve the industrial application cases of PMSMs. In this paper, we will start from the state space expression based on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha-\beta$</tex> axis to get the position angle estimation scheme of the traditional way. The traditional position angle estimation scheme pays more attention to how to extract the current information to estimate the position angle and neglects the suppression and compensation of some unknown disturbances. Therefore, the adaptive fuzzy sliding mode control will be used to suppress and compensate the unknown disturbances. Finally, the effectiveness of the above scheme is verified in different forms of simulation cases.

articleTitle: Novel Radial-Type Permanent Magnet Generators with Mechanical Flux-Weakening Design for VSCAV Control in Wind Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: This paper presents a radial-type permanent magnet (PM) generator with mechanical flux-weakening design, focusing on achieving the effect of mechanical flux-weakening through flux modulation principle, and utilizing working harmonics to determine the winding pole pair number and sequence. This design can regulate the induced back electromotive force (EMF) freely and provide a large speed range for the variable speed constant amplitude voltage (VSCAV) mode of the wind power generator. Additionally, the selection of specific working harmonics allows the generator to only require one set of windings. Two different topologies with different PM structures are presented, and their operation principles are analyzed. Finally, the two topologies are tested and compared through algorithm optimization and finite element analysis, the results show that voltage regulation ratio is about 90%, which is suitable for VSCAV control.

articleTitle: Design of Liquid Cooling System for Pouch Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on Computational Fluid Dynamics Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Maintaining lithium-ion batteries within a safe temperature range is crucial for the reliable operation of energy storage systems. Therefore, it is imperative to design a practical and efficient battery thermal management system. This paper initially conducts an experimental analysis of the heat generation characteristics of lithium-ion batteries under various discharge rates. The results show that in the range of 0.5C to 2C, with the increase of discharge rate, the temperature rise of the battery is accelerated, and the heat is mainly concentrated in the center of the electrode tabs and the core. Subsequently, a battery liquid cooling system is proposed, and the design of the liquid cooling plate is optimized according to the cells' actual heat generation characteristics. Finally, the effect of different mass flow rate concentrations on the cooling performance is investigated through numerical simulation at 2C discharge rate. The experimental results demonstrate that the implementation of this thermal management system can reduce the highest battery temperature from 35.7°C to 32.9°C, and decrease the maximum temperature difference within the battery pack to 3.3°C, thereby justifying an effective heat dissipation and ensuring the safe operation of the battery pack.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration Model of Distributed Energy Storage Location and Capacity for Distribution Station Area
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Distributed energy storage is the key technology to support the access of new energy and promote the green transformation of energy in China. The location and capacity of different distributed energy storage will significantly affect the stability of distribution network. Therefore, it is necessary to study the location and capacity of distributed energy storage in distribution station area. Considering the comprehensive cost of the whole life cycle of the energy storage system and the average outage time of the system, this paper takes the location and capacity of the energy storage system (ESS) in the distribution area with distributed generation (DG) as the research object, and proposes a distributed energy storage location and capacity optimization model based on improved particle swarm optimization algorithm, so as to achieve the goal of improving the operation economy and power supply reliability of the distribution area system. The improved IEEE-31 node distribution network is used for simulation analysis to verify the effectiveness of the optimization model proposed in this paper. The example shows that the proposed location and capacity model is solved by the improved adaptive particle swarm optimization algorithm, which can significantly reduce the installation cost of ESS, improve the DG consumption and various power supply reliability indexes.

articleTitle: Design of a Standalone EV Charger with Enhanced Control and a Wide Output Voltage Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a standalone electric vehicle (EV) charger with a wide 200V - 800V output voltage range, incorporating several features for enhanced performance. Current EV chargers face several challenges limited voltage range, high Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), and increased component count which leads to increased complexity, weight, and cost. This study aims to enhance the power quality of the EV charger while providing a wide output voltage range reducing cost and complexity. The charger, rated at 2.5kW, consists of two stages: an ACIDC stage and a DC/DC stage. The ACIDC converter regulates the input voltage to a fixed 400V DC output. The DC/DC stage either boosts or lowers the DC link voltage depending on the battery voltage. The charger achieves a wide 200V-800V output range with improved power quality, suitable for various high-voltage batteries. The proposed charger integrates the use of a phase-locked loop (PLL) and proportional resonant (PR) controller achieving significant reductions in THD from 14.92% to 2.43% at 200V and from 10.90% to 1.42% at 800V and an improved near unity power factor of 0.99998. Simulations in MATLAB/SIMULINK demon-strate improved Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and effective voltage regulation. Future work includes constructing a physical prototype to validate the simulated results.

articleTitle: Fault Ride-Through Strategy for Multiport Transformer-less Unified Power Flow Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The MTUPFC can flexibly and reliably improve the distribution of power flows in AC grids and enhance reactive power support, significantly boosting the stability and transmission capacity of the electrical system. Compared to traditional UPFCs, the MTUPFC offers several significant advantages, including not requiring transformers, being lightweight, highly efficient, cost-effective, and having easily expandable ports. However, in the event of external faults, the complex energy interactions among the MTUPFC's ports can cause fault currents to flow through healthy lines. This can lead to voltage drops at healthy ports, affecting their normal operation. This paper proposes a fault ride-through scheme for the MTUPFC that fully utilizes its active regulation capabilities to maintain voltage stability on healthy lines and achieve fault ride-through. The effectiveness of the proposed Fault Ride-Through Strategy is validated using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Feedback Type Flux-Weakening Control Using Re-Prediction of Current for Model Predictive Current Control System of PMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: This paper proposes a new feedback-type flux-weakening control method for model predictive current control systems of permanent magnet synchronous motors. The proposed method decides values of current references by using re-prediction of currents. In this paper, the validity of proposed method is demonstrated by simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: A Flux Estimator Based on Third-Order Generalized Integrators and Improved Frequency-Locked Loop for Sensorless Drive of PMSMs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Accurate flux observation is a necessary condition for high performance permanent magnet synchronous motor drive. The flux linkage can be obtained by integrating the back electromotive force (EMF), but the flux linkage obtained by traditional pure integrator, low-pass filter and second-order generalized integrator is affected by dc offset and harmonics. In addition, problems such as low order harmonics and discretization errors in electromotive force will lead to inaccurate estimation of FLL, and constant frequency estimation deviation of FLL output during motor acceleration and deceleration will lead to flux error. To solve these problems, a flux observation model based on third-order generalized integrator and improved FLL is proposed. Through theoretical research and experiments, it is proved that the proposed flux observer can provide accurate flux estimation in the range of 1–100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>rated speed.

articleTitle: Fault Protection Scheme for Multiport Transformer-less Unified Power Flow Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The traditional Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) is constructed from two back-to-back connected voltage-source converters and a pair of transformers, leading to substantial volume and high maintenance costs due to the bulky transformers. In contrast, the Multiport Transformer-less Unified Power Flow Controller (MTUPFC) not only provides decoupled control of active and reactive power flows at all terminals but also features reduced costs, smaller sizes, quicker dynamic responses, and simpler port expansion. Nevertheless, the inter-port energy coupling in MTUPFC systems can escalate the short-circuit current in non-faulty lines to flow into faulty ones during short circuits, sharply increasing fault line currents and risking irreversible damage, thus diminishing MTUPFC reliability. This paper proposes a fault protection scheme that curtails short-circuit currents and stabilizes voltage at healthy lines. This scheme limits the current by using the current limiting inductors and an active current suppression control strategy. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed fault current suppression scheme is verified by MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Gradient-Based Black-Box Modeling and Parameter Tuning for Stability Margin Improvement of Multi-Inverter System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Inverters in a power station (PS) may have different control algorithms and be made by different manufactures. To ensure small-signal stability at different equilibrium points, systematic analyses and design are required. However, analytical small-signal models of each inverter are not available to the PS operator due to intellectual property (IP), which hinders the stability analysis and improvement. To overcome this problem, firstly, a gradient-based black-box modeling technique of the inverter is proposed. The gradient-based black-box model should be provided by the manufactures. Based on it, an optimization method is proposed to improve the stability margin of the PS, which should be completed by the PS operator. Under the given work-flow, the IP rights would not be infringed.

articleTitle: The Study of Phase Change Thermal Management Schemes for Motors Under Frequent Overloads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Frequent high overload of joint motors in ex-oskeleton robots and humanoid robots is a common operating condition. Appropriate thermal design is essential to ensure the stable operation of such motors. This paper proposes a thermal management scheme for suppressing transient temperature rise by filling the motor case with phase change material (PCM). Firstly, the thermal properties of PCMs and its influence on the thermal effect of the motor are analyzed using the enthalpy-porosity model. Numerical simulation shows that the temperature rise suppression effect of PCM is only apparent after melting, and negative effects are observed before and after complete melting. Secondly, numerical models with different PCM filling thicknesses are established to analyze the effect of PCM filling amount on temperature rise. Contrary to expectations, more PCM filling does not necessarily improve the cooling effect. Under frequent high overload conditions, a smaller amount of PCM can achieve better results. The proposed minimum PCM filling scheme extends the motor overload for 6.5 s and provides a maximum temperature rise suppression capability of 10.6 K. However, too little PCM filling can have an adverse effect on the overload durability of the motor.

articleTitle: Dq-axis Current Based Protection Principle for Modular Multilevel Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: A new protection principle for modular multilevel converters based on dq-axis current is proposed. In this principle, the measured current and the calculated current on AC side of the converters are obtained together. The calculated current is derived by the relationship between the bridge arm current and AC side current of the converter. Then, three-phase currents of above two currents are transformed to dq-axis current, respectively. And the protection criterion is constructed by dq- axis current. A complete converter protection scheme that includes protection action and return logic is also designed. The proposed principle can comprehensively reflect various types of faults of converters and improve protection sensitivity using dq- axis current. The performance of the proposed protection scheme is verified by digital simulation in PSCAD. The simulation results show the effectiveness of protection principles and prove its high ability against transition resistances. The simulation also indicates that the proposed principle has a higher sensitivity than existing protections.

articleTitle: Dynamic Equivalence Study of Direct-drive Wind Farm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The large-scale integration of wind farms poses challenges to the safe and stable operation of power systems. Establishing a simulation model that accurately reflects the dynamic characteristics of wind farms is essential for power system analysis. However, detailed electromagnetic transient models of wind farms are computationally intensive and hinder further analysis. This paper addresses this issue by proposing an equivalent model that captures the response characteristics of wind farms. It examines the structure and control methods of direct-drive wind turbines, develops electromagnetic transient models for various wind turbines using PSCAD/EMTDC software, and constructs a model of an actual wind farm. The paper compares and analyzes three equivalent methods, evaluates their performance under different wind speeds and fault scenarios, and elucidates the advantages and disadvantages of these methods for wind farms with diverse turbine types.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning Control and Wave Tank Testing of Wave Energy Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The primary objective of control strategies for wave energy converters (WECs) is to optimize the conversion of wave energy into electrical power under mild wave conditions while ensuring the structural integrity and safety of the device under extreme wave conditions. Existing model-based control approaches encounter significant challenges, particularly in the accurate modeling of the system and in the prediction of wave excitation forces (WEFs). Moreover, constraints such as float displacement impose limitations on parameter selection, which in turn reduces the efficiency of energy utilization. To address these limitations, model-free control methods based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) offer a promising alternative, as they do not require precise modeling or prediction of WEFs and can efficiently handle system constraints. In this study, we propose a DRL-based control method for direct-drive point absorber WECs, utilizing the soft actor-critic (SAC) algorithm. The trained control strategies were applied to the WEC and validated through wave tank experiments. The results demonstrate that the DRL-based control strategy significantly enhances energy capture in both regular and irregular wave conditions, while strictly adhering to displacement constraints. These findings highlight the potential of the control strategy proposed as an effective tool for improving both the efficiency and safety of WEC systems.

articleTitle: Optimized Model Predictive Control Using Machine Learning for HVDC Modular Multilevel Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The modular multilevel converter (MMC) is a highly promising converter for high-voltage direct current (HVDC) systems due to its modular design and ability to manage high power levels efficiently. However, its complex dynamics demand advanced control strategies to ensure optimal performance.
