Model Predictive Control (MPC) is particularly suitable for MMCs, as it utilizes mathematical models to predict future behaviors and optimize control actions. Despite its advantages, the computational burden of MPC can limit its application in real-time scenarios requiring rapid decision-making. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes an innovative framework that integrates neural network (NN)-based machine learning (ML) techniques into the MPC framework to enhance MMC control. Neural networks, including NN regression, NN Pattern Recognition (NNPR) for regression, and NN Function Fitting (NNFF), are trained using comprehensive simulation datasets to predict optimal control actions under various conditions precisely. Simulation results show a substantial reduction in Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), illustrating the machine learning-enhanced MPC's ability to decrease computational burden while ensuring reliable MMC operation. Comparative analysis shows that NNPR for regression is the most efficient.

articleTitle: Control Strategy of Transmission Mechanism Based on Load Torque Feedforward Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: Nonlinear factors in mechanical transmission systems lead to the problem of limited control accuracy and speed. Most of the existing studies focus on the modeling and control of a single nonlinear factor, but ignore the complexity of multiple nonlinear factors in transmission mechanism, such as friction, elasticity and backlash, and so on. In this paper, a control method based on the load torque feedforward strategy is proposed. A torque observer is designed to identify load torque and reduce nonlinear effects by feedforward compensation. The simulation results show that the proposed method significantly improves the stability and speed response of the system, and effectively makes up for the shortcomings of the existing research.

articleTitle: Research on a Novel Electromechanical Booster Brake
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: With the rapid development of new-energy vehicles, the traditional vacuum brake booster no longer meets the requirements of the automobile braking system. This paper proposes a novel direct-drive and high-tracking electric brake booster system, where the hollow rotor of the booster motor is coupled with a screw to convert the motor's rotary motion into linear motion. In the structure of the new electric booster, the gear reduction mechanism or vacuum booster pump of the traditional booster is removed and the transmission link is reduced, resulting in not only a higher transmission efficiency but also a much smaller booster brake system and miniaturization of the electric booster brake system. Moreover, the structure has a redundant braking link that realizes mechanical braking in the case that the brake booster system fails. The redundant braking structure is not only highly reliable but also has a simple system structure.

articleTitle: Autonomous Vehicle Path Tracking Control Considering Yaw Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: In recent times, the use of autonomous vehicles has increased rapidly, especially in developed and developing countries. However, this increase also led to a rise in road accidents. This is because some controllers use in the control systems do not take into account the dynamic properties of the vehicle or not focusing on the dynamic stability such as roll stability which can affect overall vehicle stability. Therefore, a path tracking controller based on Model Predictive Control (MPC) was designed using a 3 degree-of-freedom (3 DOF) vehicle dynamic model. Additionally, an Integrated MPC controller is created where this is a combination of MPC and Proportional-Integral-Differential (PID) control to ensure the vehicle stability during path tracking. The performance of these controllers was evaluated through simulations in MATLAB/Simulink. This paper proposes a vehicle dynamic model using 3DOF and a powertrain model, utilizing controllers such as MPC controller, PID controller, and MPC-PID controller. The simulation begins with the testing of MPC and PID controllers separately, followed by testing the Integrated MPC-PID controller to assess their effectiveness in path tracking control. There are two scenarios used in these simulations which are the first scenario involves low vehicle speeds while the second scenario involves higher vehicle speeds. The study found that the MPC-PID controller managed to maintain the vehicle stability very well compared to other controllers at low speeds. However, in the second scenario, all controllers struggled to handle the vehicle properly, leading to roll instability especially when navigating curves.

articleTitle: Review of Frequency Response Analysis of Power Electronics-Dominated Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The growing integration of power electronic devices in power systems has brought attention to frequency stability issues due to low inertia as well as inadequate frequency regulation. In this regard, the paper defines frequency stability and introduces the frequency response process. It then outlines the current research progress in frequency response analysis methods from three perspectives: mathematical analytic algorithm, time domain simulation, and intelligent algorithms based on data-driven. The features of these modeling methods are compared in detail. Furthermore, the paper suggests future research directions and technical improvements by reviewing the frequency stability issues in power electronics-dominated power systems (PEDPSs). It is hoped that future efforts will deepen the understanding of frequency stability in PEDPSs, contributing to developing power systems with improved safety, stability, and efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on the Joint Planning of Flexible Interconnection and Energy Storage Devices in Low-Voltage Flexible Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: As human society continues to evolve, the contradiction between energy demand and supply becomes increasingly acute. New energy power generation is gradually gaining attention, with its installed capacity rapidly increasing. At the same time, many challenges have been posed to the distribution network. Low-voltage flexible interconnection devices (FIDs) can flexibly transmit power, balancing the flow of power between substations from a spatial perspective. Energy storage devices can transfer power spatially, playing a role in peak shaving and valley filling. The combination of the two can improve the power quality of low-voltage substations, enhance the capacity for distributed power absorption, and increase the power supply capability of low-voltage substations. Therefore, it is essential to study the configuration issues of low-voltage flexible interconnection devices and energy storage devices. This paper studies the joint planning of low-voltage flexible distribution substations' flexible interconnection and energy storage devices, analyzes the capacity of FID devices required for planning between low-voltage substations under different energy storage capacities, researches the joint planning strategy of FID devices and energy storage, calculates the maximum distributed photovoltaic (PV) carrying capacity of each substation under different planning schemes, analyzes indicators such as voltage deviation and network loss, and finally verifies the effectiveness of the model in a low-voltage substation distribution system with different load types.

articleTitle: Lithium-Ion Battery Pack State of Charge Balance Based on Reconfigurable Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The individual cells of lithium-ion battery packs cause inconsistency in the battery packs due to production differences. The working environment further aggravates the inconsistency of the battery packs, which seriously affects the efficiency and service life. To improve the consistency of battery packs, the four-switch reconfigurable cells are proposed in this paper; Heuristic algorithms are proposed to determine the switching states to obtain a battery topology that satisfies the requirements. This minimises the mismatch between the target load voltage and the output voltage of the battery pack and maintains the State of Charge (SOC) balance between different cells. The core of the proposed reconfiguration strategy is to divide all normal battery cells into modules when output voltage requirements are met. The modules are connected in parallel within the modules and in series between the modules so that all the battery cells are kept charged and discharged at the same rate. The results show that after reconfigurable balance, the energy utilization efficiency of the battery pack reaches 86.08%. The deviation of the SOC of the battery pack is reduced by 62.15%. It indicates that the inconsistency of the battery pack has been greatly improved.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis and Judgment Based on Virtual Synchronous Generator Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Electrical Energy Conversion Systems and Control（IEECSC)
abstract: The Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) technology, which draws on the operating mechanism of traditional synchronous generators, has important research significance for improving the grid stability of microgrids, but VSG faces transient stability problems similar to those of conventional synchronous generators, and the strong nonlinearity of VSG makes their transient stability analysis more complicated. Therefore, in this paper, starting from the synchronous generator power angle differential equation, an improved multiscale method is used to obtain the explicit analytical solution of the second-order nonlinear differential equation of the power angle, and the analytical solution is used to quantitatively analyze the effects of the VSG control parameters with respect to the stability of transient synchronization. Second, the synchronization stability is determined on the basis of the transient stability condition and according to the analytical solution. Finally, the analytical model and the validity of the stability determination method are verified by simulation.
